exact_substitutions.before: Example ($\gamma=0.9$). The limit is $10$. With $0.9^{10}=0.3487$, the first ten terms give $S_{10}=6.513$ and the tail is $3.487$. Capturing $99\%$ needs $\gamma^T\le0.01$, i.e. $T\ge\ln0.01/\ln0.9=43.7$: $44$ terms. Because $\ln(1/\gamma)\ge1-\gamma$ (proved below), $T\ge\ln(1/\varepsilon)/(1-\gamma)$ always guarantees $\gamma^T\le\varepsilon$; here it asks for $47$. The explorer's lower panel computes this for any $\gamma$.
